Overview

KUJO — Trust at the speed of AI.

18-slide investor briefing with source evidence, recorded execution and editable planning assumptions.

1. Trust at the speed of AI.

The programming language and accountability infrastructure for agent-driven development.

    Investor briefing / November 2026

    2. Software production is outpacing verification.

    Agents can report completion. Teams still need a reviewable chain from requested work to release decision.

    1. 01

      The claim

      “Tests passed. Ready to merge.” An illustrative agent statement.

    2. 02

      The evidence

      Command, exit code, changed revision, environment and retained failure output.

    3. 03

      The gap

      Useful logs already exist. Connecting them across tools and review boundaries remains work.

    02 / The accountability problem

    Thesis · existing agent controls acknowledged

    3. Greater autonomy requires stronger accountability.

    The cost of an unverified action grows as agents gain authority.

    1. 01

      Suggest code

      Human selects the change → diff review

    2. 02

      Complete a task

      Agent edits and runs commands → execution records

    3. 03

      Operate a workflow

      Retries and external effects → boundaries, recovery and approval

    03 / Structural shift

    Conceptual progression; not a measured adoption curve

    4. AI use is broad. Trust remains conditional.

    Adoption of AI assistance is not evidence of autonomous production deployment.

    use coding assistants or coding agents at work
    65.9%
    use AI agents or automated workflows at work
    26.2%
    trust AI when answers are easy to validate
    48%

      04 / Why now

      M03–M04 · Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2026

      5. Build with clarity. Operate with control.

      The language is the long-term foundation. Existing tools offer an earlier route into engineering workflows.

      1. 01

        Clarity

        Kujo language / Spec / Eval: explicit intent and testable outcomes.

      2. 02

        Context

        MCP / CaseFile / RunLedger: useful inputs, debugging evidence and run records.

      3. 03

        Control

        Dispatch / Workcell / ShipCheck: orchestration, bounded execution and release checks.

      05 / The Kujo system

      T01–T14 · tool boundaries remain distinct

      6. Accountability spans the whole task.

      Each component owns a specific responsibility. A reviewable workflow composes their artifacts explicitly.

      1. 01

        Instruction → Context

        Spec / PackWrite → MCP and repository context

      2. 02

        Execution → Evaluation

        Dispatch / Workcell → Eval result artifacts

      3. 03

        Evidence → Review → Release

        CaseFile / RunLedger → reviewer → ShipCheck gate

      06 / Lifecycle

      Composition map; not automatic end-to-end enforcement

      7. The foundation is already being built.

      Inspect the implementation and its limits, then reproduce the smallest useful proof.

      1. 01

        Language and VM

        Kujo 1.9.0 is documented; a local 1.9.0 binary executes the recorded fixture tooling.

      2. 02

        Bounded execution

        Workcell 1.3 documents Docker/Podman limits, explicit exports and receipt verification.

      3. 03

        Reviewable artifact

        This presentation uses the native Kujo builder. Its demo retains a failing command, correction and evaluation.

      07 / Engineering proof

      T01, T03, T08, T14 · release documentation ≠ all HEAD features

      8. A claim becomes inspectable evidence.

      Recorded local coding fixture: correct a post-money ownership calculation. Inspect what failed, what changed and what passed.

      1. 01

        Request

        Return 20% for $6M raised at $30M post-money.

      2. 02

        Execution

        CaseFile captures real Node assertion failure and corrected execution.

      3. 03

        Decision

        Eval checks the correction. Accept this fixture; no production release.

      08 / Recorded demonstration

      Assistant-authored seeded fixture · CaseFile + Eval · local host

      9. Adopt the ecosystem before the language.

      Keep application code in its existing language. Introduce accountability at the workflow boundary.

      1. 01

        Today: wrap the task

        Use CaseFile for command evidence and Eval for explicit repository checks.

      2. 02

        Then: control execution

        Adopt Dispatch or Workcell after validating the target environment and runtime pins.

      3. 03

        Over time: go deeper

        Choose Kujo for new agent tooling where native language integration adds value.

      09 / Adoption without migration

      T02–T04, T08 · tools have their own runtime dependencies

      10. Start with teams already delegating engineering work.

      Proposed beachhead: agent-platform builders shipping repeatable engineering workflows.

      1. 01

        Buyer / user

        Platform engineering lead / engineers operating coding-agent harnesses.

      2. 02

        Immediate pain

        Failed runs are expensive to reconstruct. Review spans commits, logs and agent transcripts.

      3. 03

        Purchase hypothesis

        Pay for retained evidence, controlled execution and team review if they reduce investigation time.

      10 / Initial customer

      Proposed segment; no customer interviews or demand validation

      11. Open tooling can lead to a commercial operating layer.

      Earn developer trust through useful local tools. Charge for shared operational responsibilities.

      1. 01

        Available foundation

        Open repositories and local developer tooling.

      2. 02

        Proposed team service

        Hosted evidence, retention, shared review and execution capacity.

      3. 03

        Proposed enterprise tier

        Organization policy, deployment controls, support and governance.

      11 / Business model

      Hosted offerings and pricing are proposals, not available SKUs

      12. A focused entry market can support a meaningful business.

      Illustrative bottom-up model. Organization counts and annual contracts are assumptions to validate.

      initial target organizations × $24K ACV
      2,000
      illustrative annual serviceable revenue pool
      $48M
      100 customers × $24K; milestone scenario, not forecast
      $2.4M

        12 / Market model

        Planning only · editable assumptions in appendix

        13. Accountability requires more than generating code.

        Existing platforms are strong. Kujo must win on useful evidence and the cost of operating reliable workflows.

        1. 01

          Coding agents / GitHub

          Generation, repository context and review are already integrated into major developer surfaces.

        2. 02

          Orchestration / LangGraph

          Persistence, recovery and human review are established capabilities.

        3. 03

          Kujo opportunity

          Connect explicit contracts, bounded work and inspectable artifacts. Prove adoption before claiming a moat.

        13 / Position and defensibility

        C01–C02, T01–T14 · no exclusivity or benchmark superiority

        14. Meet developers inside their existing workflows.

        The planned December 2026 open-source campaign should produce repeat usage and customer learning.

        1. 01

          Discovery

          GitHub releases, technical demos, docs and reproducible fixtures → qualified visits.

        2. 02

          Activation

          Agent harness recipes and MCP tooling → first successful evidence run.

        3. 03

          Retention → revenue

          Repeat weekly runs → design-partner discussions → paid pilots and renewal evidence.

        14 / Distribution

        Campaign and partnerships planned; measure cohorts, not raw impressions

        15. Execution is visible. Demand still needs proof.

        Engineering output, external adoption and commercial traction are different measures.

        1. 01

          Engineering output

          Public repositories, documented releases and the locally reproduced evidence fixture.

        2. 02

          External adoption

          Verified outside usage, retention and independent integrations: data not supplied.

        3. 03

          Commercial traction

          Design partners, paying customers and revenue: data not supplied. Complete before investor distribution.

        15 / Momentum

        Unavailable is not zero; no invented traction

        16. Built through sustained open-source engineering.

        Robert DeVore connects open-web product work with a growing language and developer-tooling ecosystem.

        1. 01

          Background

          Public biography describes years of WordPress, WooCommerce, plugins and publishing systems.

        2. 02

          Current work

          Language/runtime infrastructure, orchestration, evaluation, telemetry and evidence workflows.

        3. 03

          Team enabled by capital

          Proposed hires in runtime, execution reliability and developer experience; later customer engineering.

        16 / Founder and team

        F01 · first-person source; no invented tenure, team or security credentials

        17. Capital turns a technical foundation into an adopted platform.

        Working seed scenario. Financing terms and hiring pace remain assumptions.

        target raise
        $6M
        post-money valuation or SAFE cap assumption
        $30M
        planned runway, including reserve
        24 mo

          17 / Investment and milestones

          20% simplified ownership before further dilution · $150K founder annual base

          18. Agents will build more software.

          The organizations deploying it will still be accountable for what it does.

            18 / The vision

            KUJO · Trust at the speed of AI.

DILIGENCE / 01

One ecosystem. Separate responsibilities.

The architecture below is a composition map. Solid associations describe documented responsibilities; the hosted operating layer is proposed. No automatic universal integration or policy enforcement is claimed.

Clarity: intent and outcome

Kujo compiler/runtime runs programs. Spec defines task contracts. Eval executes configured checks. Language capability policies do not replace container or operating-system boundaries.

Context: inputs and records

MCP exposes configured tools/resources. CaseFile captures commands and logs. RunLedger stores supplied results and Git context. Watchdog records supported telemetry and estimated costs.

Control: state and execution

Dispatch persists workflow state and approvals. Workcell applies supported host/container limits. ShipCheck checks release-readiness signals. Human reviewers retain authority.

Proposed commercial layer

Hosted execution, evidence retention, team review and organization governance. Product integration, multi-tenant isolation, service operations and commercial validation remain work to fund.

DILIGENCE / 04

A correctness fixture, not a performance claim

Method: Node assertions check 6/30 = 20% and 3/30 = 10%; the initial denominator intentionally adds the raise and fails. CaseFile captures both executions. Eval runs the assertion command and checks the corrected source expression. Observed result: two configured Eval checks passed, with the earlier assertion failure retained.

Reproduce with python3 scripts/record-demo.py from the source deck, using the sibling CaseFile, Eval and Kujo 1.9.0 checkout. This overwrites the recorded fixture artifacts; retain the original before comparing runs. Timings are recorded but not a statistically meaningful benchmark. No competitor benchmark, latency advantage, comprehensive correctness or security certification is claimed.

Future benchmark plan: publish fixed repositories, pinned environments, task corpus, failure taxonomy, complete attempts, repeated seeds and independent reproduction. Measure reviewer time, evidence completeness and failure recovery alongside task success.

Funding scenarios and dilution

Working scenario: $6M at $30M post-money. These are planning inputs, not agreed terms or validated valuation. Simplified ownership = raise ÷ post-money; SAFE mechanics, option pools and other instruments can change outcomes.

At fixed $30M post-money: $3M → 10%; $6M → 20%; $8M → 26.67%; $10M → 33.33%. A later round that dilutes all holders by 20% reduces a 20% holding to 16%.

$3M prioritizes one flagship workflow and a smaller team. $6M supports parallel runtime, execution and developer experience work. $8M/$10M permit more integration and commercial capacity, conditional on evidence of demand.
